title: Thistledown Press 'The Lantern Fox' KDP picture book: neutralize a two-session illustration-scan set to one page-white, match the fox's scarf to one house crimson across scans, prep-and-vectorize the imprint mark, then data-merge the illustrated interior and the wraparound cover to press PDF

source.reference: KDP Formatter Needed for 32-Page Children's Picture Book — Paperback

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief (a self-publisher wanting 'a professional formatter to prepare paperback print-ready files for Amazon KDP' for a children's picture book: interior formatted to an 8.5x11 in trim, 'Bleed, margins, and resolution set to KDP specifications', a 'Full wraparound cover file with correct spine width', and files that 'pass KDP's preflight check first time'). The client and title are laundered to a fictional imprint, THISTLEDOWN PRESS, and a fictional book, 'The Lantern Fox' — no real publisher, book, illustrator, person, or trademark is named; Amazon KDP is a real self-publishing channel used only as the delivery target (allowed), and Adobe / InDesign is the platform. The killed version of this slot was a preflight AUDIT that produced a findings report and pre-announced its own planted defects; it is REPLACED here with the BUILD the brief actually pays for. The from-scratch page composition of a picture book is out of connector scope, so the client is modeled as supplying the two authored InDesign shells that make the job connector-legal — a single-record illustrated-interior-page template (.indd with a full-bleed @illustration image column and live <<page_no>>/<<caption>>/<<line2>> caption fields) and a single-record wraparound-cover template (.indd with @cover_art + @wordmark image columns and <<title>>/<<author>>/<<spine_text>>/<<back_blurb>> fields, its spine sized for the page count) — plus the raw materials the freelancer must actually finish: ten high-resolution art-reproduction scans of the physical gouache illustrations captured across two sessions under mismatched light (each with a photographic neutral grey step-wedge laid on the scan bed), the front-cover painting scan, the imprint wordmark inked on paper, the story-caption CSV, and the one-row cover CSV. The Adobe chain does the real creative work: neutralize every illustration scan to its own in-frame grey wedge so the whole book prints at one page-white, hold the one nightfall illustration's intentional amber instead of 'correcting' it, bring the fox's red scarf to one consistent house crimson across three scans shot in different sessions, prep-and-vectorize the imprint mark, then run the authored templates through one-record-per-page data-merges and export the illustrated interior and the wraparound cover as press-ready PDFs.
one_line_ask: Take ten mixed-lighting art-repro scans of 'The Lantern Fox' gouache illustrations (each carrying a grey step-wedge), neutralize each to its wedge so the book prints at one page-white, hold the nightfall page's intended amber, match the fox's red scarf to one house crimson across the three scans it appears in, prep-and-vectorize the Thistledown imprint mark, then data-merge the client's authored interior and wraparound-cover templates to produce the press-ready 10-page illustrated interior PDF (one page per caption row) and the wraparound cover PDF.
full_brief: Thistledown Press is a small independent children's-book imprint about to upload its next paperback, 'The Lantern Fox', to Amazon KDP. The last title we sent up bounced in preflight because the interior pages did not print consistently and the cover art was off, so this time we want a print specialist to actually FINISH the files, not just check them. The manuscript, the caption text, and all the artwork already exist — we are NOT re-illustrating and we do NOT want anything redrawn. Here is the situation and what a print-ready result has to look like. First, the illustrations. Our illustrator painted the story in gouache and we scanned the ten story-page paintings, but not all in one sitting: half were captured on the flatbed one afternoon (they come out cool and slightly blue) and half were shot on the copy stand another evening under our old warm work lights (they come out warm and orange), and a few of the paintings sat a little crooked when they were captured. On the scan bed beside every painting we laid a photographic neutral grey step-wedge so there is an honest reference to balance against. Straight out of the folder the set is a jumble — the same cream page-paper looks blue in one scan and amber in the next — and a picture book whose pages don't share a page-white looks cheap and gets rejected. Your job on the artwork: bring every scan to a consistent, true look by neutralizing each one to the grey wedge it carries, so the wedge reads as a clean neutral and, once every wedge is neutral, the whole book shares ONE page-white. Each painting was lit differently and needs its OWN white-balance and exposure decision to land there — do not force one blanket correction across the batch. Be careful with the nightfall page ('the fox on the starlit hill'): that illustration is SUPPOSED to glow warm amber from the lantern, and it was captured cleanly so its grey wedge already reads neutral — do NOT cool it chasing an imagined orange cast or you will kill the mood the whole book builds to. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each scan so we can confirm the set is genuinely matched, not eyeballed. Second, continuity: the fox wears a red scarf, and because the three pages it appears on came from different sessions the scarf currently reads cold-maroon on one page, muddy on the dark hollow-tree page, and orange on the warm market page. Bring the scarf to ONE consistent house crimson on all three — a rich true red in the same family, deepened or warmed just enough to match, riding the real folds and shadow of the cloth, not a flat painted patch and not a tint that bleeds onto the fox or the background. Third, our imprint colophon only exists as the mark inked on a piece of off-white paper; get it clean and razor-sharp as scalable art for the cover and title page — it must not look like a fuzzy scan when printed. Finally, build the files. We have hand-built two InDesign shells: an illustrated-interior-page template with a full-bleed picture frame and the caption type fields, and a wraparound-cover template (back, spine, front on one sheet) with the spine already sized for our page count. We are giving you the story-caption sheet (one row per illustrated page, in reading order) and the cover sheet. Merge them: drop each finished illustration into its page with the caption bound from our sheet, and build the wraparound cover with the finished cover painting, the vectorized imprint mark, and the title and back-cover copy in place. Hand back the illustrated interior as ONE press-ready PDF with one page per caption row at KDP's 8.5x11 in trim with 0.125 in bleed and 300 DPI artwork, and the wraparound cover as its own press-ready PDF. Bind our caption and cover copy verbatim — do not rewrite it. Acceptance: every grey wedge neutral and the set matched to one page-white; the scarf one crimson on all three pages; the imprint mark a crisp vector; and exactly one interior page per caption row.

inputs.name: illustration_scans_x10.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 10 high-resolution art-reproduction captures of PHYSICAL gouache children's-book paintings for 'The Lantern Fox', each ~3600 px on the short edge and ~4600 px on the long edge (full-resolution flatbed scans / copy-stand camera stills straight off the device, well above the 2625x3375 px an 8.5x11 in + 0.125 in bleed page needs at 300 DPI so every crop is a DOWNSCALE), each with a photographic neutral grey step-wedge and a small white strip laid flat on the scan bed alongside the painting as a reference. Captured across two sessions under mismatched light. SESSION A (flatbed, cool bluish cast): (1) il01_fox_meadow — the fox in a spring meadow wearing a RED SCARF, cool cast, level; (2) il02_riverbank — the fox at a riverbank, cool cast, painting sat ~3 deg crooked on the bed; (3) il03_hollow_tree — the fox inside a dark hollow tree at dusk wearing the RED SCARF, cool cast, a dim underexposed interior scene; (4) il04_snowfield — the fox crossing a bright white snowfield, cool cast, near-neutral and white-dominant; (5) il05_starlit_hill — THE NIGHTFALL PAGE: the fox on a starlit hill holding a glowing lantern, intentionally warm amber lantern-glow by artistic design, captured cleanly so its grey step-wedge already reads neutral (the warmth is the painting, not a cast), level. SESSION B (copy stand, warm tungsten cast): (6) il06_market_lane — the fox in a lantern-lit market lane wearing the RED SCARF, warm cast, bright, level; (7) il07_lantern_shop — the fox in a lantern shop, warm cast, painting sat ~4 deg crooked; (8) il08_rooftops — the fox on moonlit rooftops, warm cast, overexposed with near-blown highlights; (9) il09_bridge_fog — the fox on a foggy bridge, warm cast, flat and low-contrast; (10) il10_homecoming — the fox arriving home at the lit doorway, warm cast, level. Real gouache brush and paper texture, visible tooth of the illustration board, no digital gloss, no CGI. The grey step-wedge is clearly visible and uncropped in every scan.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL art-repro capture at ~3600x4600 px (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each full-bleed portrait crop fills the 8.5x11 in + bleed page frame at >=300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere in the chain. Deliberately mismatched by session (cool flatbed vs warm copy-stand, plus per-scan exposure and tilt variance) so a single blanket correction cannot match the set — each scan needs its own decision, driven to its in-frame grey step-wedge (the free, checkable neutral target). il05 is the TRAP: its amber is the real painting and its wedge already reads neutral, so cooling it is wrong. il01/il03/il06 carry the RED SCARF and, coming from different sessions, start at three different reds — they must converge on one house crimson. Delivered as a zip of 10 individually addressable full-resolution files (il01_fox_meadow ... il10_homecoming).

inputs.name: lanternfox_cover_art.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A high-resolution art-reproduction capture of the PHYSICAL gouache FRONT-COVER painting for 'The Lantern Fox' — the fox holding its lantern beneath a big harvest moon, portrait orientation — ~4000 px on the short edge and ~5000 px on the long edge (full-resolution, well above what an 8.75x11.25 in front panel needs at 300 DPI so the crop is a downscale), captured on the warm copy-stand session with a warm tungsten cast, a photographic neutral grey step-wedge laid on the bed at the frame edge. Real gouache texture, board tooth, no digital gloss, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: The hero cover painting, camera-scale so the full-bleed front-panel crop is downscale-only. Carries its own grey step-wedge so it is neutralized to the same page-white family as the interior before it is placed; the warm cover-art capture must be balanced without stripping the intended harvest-moon warmth. Supplied, not chain-generated.

inputs.name: thistledown_imprint_mark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the THISTLEDOWN PRESS imprint colophon inked on off-white textured paper: a small thistle glyph above a hand-lettered condensed-serif wordmark reading 'THISTLEDOWN PRESS', deep ink on a warm off-white (cream) paper ground (NOT transparent, NOT pure white). Rendered as a real scan — the mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize crisply.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2 deg skew, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper rectangle and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace (straighten -> crisp/drop the ground -> crop to the mark -> knock the off-white to transparency -> vectorize). gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering; vector output is resolution-independent so camera scale is not required here.

inputs.name: lanternfox_interior_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE illustrated interior page of an 8.5x11 in (US Letter portrait) KDP paperback picture book — ONE story page per record. It carries a FULL-BLEED image frame (extending to the 0.125 in bleed on all outer edges) wired to an @-prefixed image-path merge column named @illustration so the merge drops each finished painting into the page, plus live InDesign data-merge caption fields <<page_no>>, <<caption>>, and <<line2>> placed in a caption text frame inside the 0.375 in safe margin. Built by hand in InDesign so the fields and the @image frame actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (fields would not bind) and NOT a multi-record N-up spread: document_merge_data_layout emits one page per row, so the template holds exactly one page's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus a genuine @image-path column, and it produces ONE PAGE PER ROW — so a single illustrated-page template merged against the 10-row caption sheet yields the 10-page illustrated interior. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal text would not bind. The full-bleed @illustration frame is the only connector-legal way to place the finished paintings into laid-out pages.

inputs.name: lanternfox_story_captions.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns page_no,caption,line2,@illustration holding 10 rows, one per illustrated story page of 'The Lantern Fox' IN READING ORDER, each with a short children's-book caption (<<caption>>) and an optional short second line (<<line2>>). Row order and the @illustration cells map each page to its finished painting: row 1 -> @il01_fox_meadow.jpg, row 2 -> @il02_riverbank.jpg, row 3 -> @il03_hollow_tree.jpg, row 4 -> @il04_snowfield.jpg, row 5 -> @il05_starlit_hill.jpg, row 6 -> @il06_market_lane.jpg, row 7 -> @il07_lantern_shop.jpg, row 8 -> @il08_rooftops.jpg, row 9 -> @il09_bridge_fog.jpg, row 10 -> @il10_homecoming.jpg. Column names must exactly match the interior template merge fields <<page_no>>,<<caption>>,<<line2>> and the @illustration image-path column.
inputs.realism_notes: One row per illustrated page in reading order; headers match the authored interior .indd fields and the @illustration column so the one-page-per-row [T] merge binds each caption AND drops the correct finished painting. Ten rows => the merge must produce exactly ten interior pages (page-count == row-count == 10 is the acceptance gate). The @illustration cells resolve to the agent's own graded/cropped page images.

inputs.name: lanternfox_cover_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD wraparound KDP paperback cover — back panel, spine, and front panel laid left-to-right on ONE flattened sheet at the correct wraparound trim with 0.125 in bleed all around, the narrow spine already sized for the book's page count. It carries TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns — @cover_art (a full-bleed image frame on the FRONT panel) and @wordmark (a small image frame for the imprint mark on the spine/back) — and live data-merge text fields <<title>>, <<author>>, <<spine_text>>, and <<back_blurb>>. Built by hand in InDesign so the two image frames and the text fields bind; InDesign data merge supports multiple @-image columns in one template. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output.
inputs.realism_notes: The wraparound cover is a genuine authored single-record .indd; a one-row cover CSV merged through it places the finished cover painting and the vectorized imprint mark and sets the title/author/back copy, and document_render_layout then exports the one-page wraparound cover to press PDF. Supplied, not chain-generated. Two @-image columns (art + mark) is standard InDesign data-merge and the only connector-legal way to place the agent's produced cover art and vector mark into the laid-out cover.

inputs.name: lanternfox_cover_data.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a single-row CSV with columns title,author,spine_text,back_blurb,@cover_art,@wordmark for 'The Lantern Fox'. title='The Lantern Fox'; author a fictional illustrator/author name; spine_text a short spine line ('The Lantern Fox  •  Thistledown Press'); back_blurb a 2-3 sentence children's-book back-cover blurb. @cover_art resolves to the finished front-cover painting the agent produces; @wordmark resolves to the vectorized imprint mark. Column names must exactly match the cover template's <<title>>,<<author>>,<<spine_text>>,<<back_blurb>> fields and the @cover_art / @wordmark image columns.
inputs.realism_notes: One row => one wraparound cover page. Headers match the authored cover .indd fields and the two @-image columns so the [T] merge binds the copy and places the agent's finished cover art and vector mark. Copy binds verbatim; no copywriting is invented by the connector.

outputs.name: LanternFox_Interior_Press.pdf
outputs.spec: The primary owned artifact: a press-ready illustrated interior PDF exported from the one-page-per-row InDesign data-merge — EXACTLY ten pages, one story page per caption row (page-count == row-count == 10) in reading order — each page carrying its finished, grey-wedge-neutralized full-bleed painting dropped through the @illustration frame (filling the 8.5x11 in trim to the 0.125 in bleed) with <<page_no>>/<<caption>>/<<line2>> typeset verbatim from the caption sheet inside the 0.375 in safe margin. Acceptance: 300 DPI effective artwork resolution at trim, bleed carried on all outer edges, and every page sharing one page-white (the same corrected page-paper tone across all ten).

outputs.name: LanternFox_Cover_Wrap.pdf
outputs.spec: The owned wraparound-cover artifact: a single-page press-ready wraparound cover PDF exported from the one-row cover merge — back panel, spine, front panel on one sheet with 0.125 in bleed — carrying the finished, neutralized cover painting placed full-bleed on the front through @cover_art, the vectorized imprint mark placed through @wordmark, and <<title>>/<<author>>/<<spine_text>>/<<back_blurb>> typeset verbatim. Acceptance: one wraparound page, cover art at >=300 DPI at trim, the imprint mark placed as crisp vector.

outputs.name: graded_masters_x10
outputs.spec: The RETAINED card-bearing neutralized masters and the artifact neutrality is graded on: ten straightened-where-needed FULL-FRAME illustration masters (il01_master..il10_master), each STILL CARRYING its in-frame grey step-wedge, neutralized so the wedge reads a clean neutral (R=G=B) and the whole set matched to ONE page-white while the nightfall page (il05) holds its intended amber; the fox's red scarf resolved to one house crimson on the three masters it appears on (il01/il03/il06). These are the neutralized (and, for il01/il03/il06, scarf-corrected) full-frame chain outputs BEFORE the page crop — il01_house/il02_neutral/il03_house/il04_neutral/il05_neutral/il06_house/il07_neutral/il08_neutral/il09_neutral/il10_neutral — retained/exported as a real deliverable. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each scan and the three scarf HSL moves. Acceptance (grader-checked ON THESE, wedge in frame): every grey step-wedge neutral within a tight per-channel spread and the set matched to one page-white; il05 wedge held neutral with its amber intact. Neutrality is NEVER graded on the card-cropped page crops.

outputs.name: graded_illustrations_x10
outputs.spec: The ten card-cropped full-bleed portrait PAGE CROPS (il01_page..il10_page) derived by downscale from graded_masters_x10 — each cropped to the 8.75x11.25 in (incl. bleed) page frame with the fox held in the KDP safe area and the grey step-wedge cropped OUT of frame in the same move. These are the page images the @illustration column binds. Because the wedge is gone from these files, neutrality is NOT graded here; it is graded on graded_masters_x10. The only card-related check on these crops is card-EXCLUSION. Acceptance (grader-checked): full-bleed portrait crop at >=300 DPI effective at trim, downscale-only from the camera-scale master (never upscaled/extended), the grey step-wedge fully EXCLUDED from the delivered frame, and the crop carrying its master's neutralization plus (for il01/il03/il06) the one house-crimson scarf.

outputs.name: thistledown_imprint_mark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the Thistledown Press imprint colophon (thistle glyph + wordmark), traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at cover/title-page scale with no captured paper ground or skew. Placed into the cover through the @wordmark column and delivered as a standalone asset.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: illustration_scans_x10.zip, lanternfox_cover_art.jpg, thistledown_imprint_mark_scan.png, lanternfox_interior_template.indd, lanternfox_story_captions.csv, lanternfox_cover_template.indd, lanternfox_cover_data.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the ten illustration scans, the cover painting, the imprint-mark scan, both authored .indd templates and both CSVs into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. Single upload — plumbing, not the difficulty.

Session A, cool bluish cast, level. WARM the temperature and set tint until the in-frame grey step-wedge reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure to bring the cream page-paper to the shared page-white and hold gentle contrast/clarity. Reason the exact temp/tint/exposure to THIS wedge — do not reuse another scan's numbers. Report the final move. Primitive-built adjustment (replaces deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _brightness_and_contrast).

Triage: this painting sat ~3 deg crooked on the bed, so level it BEFORE grading and cropping (deciding which scans are crooked and which are level is part of the job — only il02 and il07 get straightened).
Session A, cool cast. Warm to neutralize its grey wedge to the shared page-white, match set brightness. Distinct numbers from il01 because the light differed. Report the move.

Session A, cool cast, a dim underexposed interior scene. Warm to neutralize its grey wedge AND LIFT exposure/shadows to reach the shared page-white without crushing the dark hollow-tree interior to black. The dominant move here is tonal as well as WB — a different problem from il01. Report the move.

Session A, cool cast, near-neutral and white-dominant (snowfield). A SMALL warm nudge to neutralize the wedge is enough; over-correcting drives the snow warm or clips it. Protect the white snow from clipping to 255 while landing the wedge neutral. Restraint case. Report the (small) move.

THE TRAP PAGE. The nightfall scene is intentionally warm amber (the lantern glow) and it was captured cleanly so its grey step-wedge ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is to HOLD white balance (no cooling) and only match the page-white/exposure lightly against the wedge. A naive agent that batch-applies the Session-A 'warm the cool cast' move, or that 'cools an imagined orange cast', will push the wedge off-neutral and strip the amber mood the whole book builds to. Decision driven by THIS wedge, not the batch. Report that WB was held.

Session B, warm tungsten cast, bright, level. This scan must move the OPPOSITE direction from the Session-A frames: COOL the temperature (negative) and pull exposure DOWN until its grey wedge reads neutral and it matches the shared page-white. Adaptive — a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here. Report the move.
Triage: this painting sat ~4 deg crooked — level it before grading and cropping.
Session B, warm cast. Cool to neutralize its grey wedge to the shared page-white. Report the move.

Session B, warm cast, overexposed with near-blown highlights. PULL exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the moonlit rooftops, then cool to neutralize its grey wedge to the shared page-white. Opposite tonal direction from the underexposed il03. Report the move.
Session B, warm cast, flat and low-contrast (fog). ADD contrast and cool to neutralize its grey wedge to the shared page-white without muddying the fog. Report the move.

Session B, warm cast, level. Cool to neutralize its grey wedge to the shared page-white; protect the lit-doorway highlight. Report the move. All ten wedges now read neutral at one shared page-white, each corrected on its own decision.

Scarf-continuity pass, il01: semantically select ONLY the fox's red scarf ('the red scarf worn by the fox') so the recolor is confined to the cloth and never touches the fox, meadow or grey wedge. Returns a maskURI. Not a hue/coordinate selection — a real object.

Masked recolor on il01's scarf: from the cold-maroon start, a SMALL within-family hue nudge toward the house crimson plus a saturation/luminance settle so it lands on the shared crimson target — an in-band adjacent shift (well under ~60 deg, staying in the red family; NOT a near-complementary rotation), riding the cloth's existing luminosity so folds and shadow stay natural. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image and image_fill_area is flat dead-fill — both wrong here.
Scarf-continuity pass, il03: select only the fox's red scarf in the dark hollow-tree scene. Returns a maskURI.

Masked recolor on il03's scarf: from the muddy-dark red, lift saturation and nudge hue within the red band to the SAME house crimson target as il01, letting the existing luminosity carry the folds in the dim scene. Cross-scan color match to a common target — the measurable continuity core. In-band shift, not a rotation to a new hue.
Scarf-continuity pass, il06: select only the fox's red scarf in the warm market-lane scene. Returns a maskURI.

Masked recolor on il06's scarf: from the warm orange-red start, nudge hue back toward true crimson and trim saturation to land on the SAME house crimson target used for il01 and il03, so the scarf reads identical across all three sessions. In-family deepen-and-settle riding the original luminosity — not a jump to a far-off hue.

Crop to the full-bleed portrait page frame (8.75x11.25 in incl. bleed, ~2625x3375 px at 300 DPI): subject-aware so the fox stays in the KDP safe area, and crop the grey step-wedge OUT of frame in the same move. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the ~3600x4600 source — never canvas-extend, never upscale. Feeds the @il01 cell.
Crop to the full-bleed portrait page frame, fox in safe area, wedge cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds @il02.
Crop to the full-bleed portrait page frame, wedge cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds @il03.
Crop to the full-bleed portrait page frame, wedge cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds @il04.
Crop the amber-held nightfall page to the full-bleed portrait frame, wedge cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds @il05.
Crop to the full-bleed portrait page frame, wedge cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds @il06.
Crop to the full-bleed portrait page frame, wedge cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds @il07.
Crop to the full-bleed portrait page frame, wedge cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds @il08.
Crop to the full-bleed portrait page frame, wedge cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds @il09.

Crop to the full-bleed portrait page frame, wedge cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds @il10. Steps 20-29 produce the card-cropped page crops (graded_illustrations_x10) and the ten @illustration cells the interior merge binds. The card-bearing masters are the pre-crop neutralized/scarf-corrected full-frame outputs (il01_house/il02_neutral/il03_house/il04_neutral/il05_neutral/il06_house/il07_neutral/il08_neutral/il09_neutral/il10_neutral) from steps 2-19, which are RETAINED as graded_masters_x10 with the grey wedge still in frame — neutrality is graded on those masters, never on these wedge-cropped crops.

Grade the warm cover painting: cool the tungsten cast to neutralize its grey step-wedge to the same page-white family as the interior, but HOLD the intended harvest-moon warmth in the art itself (balance the neutral reference, not the mood). Report the move.

Crop the neutralized cover painting to the full-bleed FRONT-panel frame (8.75x11.25 in incl. bleed), fox+lantern in the safe area, grey wedge cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the ~4000x5000 source. Feeds the @cover_art cell.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the imprint scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.
Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the warm off-white paper toward white so the ink separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the thistle glyph + wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms and glyph only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill, which would flat-fill and destroy the counters in the lettering).

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the cover and title page. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. DELIVERABLE thistledown_imprint_mark.svg; also feeds the @wordmark cell.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: lanternfox_interior_template.indd, lanternfox_story_captions.csv, il01_page, il02_page, il03_page, il04_page, il05_page, il06_page, il07_page, il08_page, il09_page, il10_page
connector_workflow.note: [T] One-page-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the ten caption rows (page_no/caption/line2) into the authored single-page interior .indd's live <<fields>> and drop that row's finished painting into the full-bleed @illustration frame, producing EXACTLY ONE interior page per row (ten pages) in reading order. Requires the hand-authored template — a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind, and document_merge_data_vector is text-only and could not place the @illustration image.

Export the merged interior to a press-ready PDF at KDP's 8.5x11 in trim with 0.125 in bleed and 300 DPI artwork — one page per story row. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document in a single call (no per-page named export). Acceptance: page-count == row-count == 10; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed. PRIMARY DELIVERABLE.

[T] One-row wraparound-cover merge: bind the single cover row (<<title>>/<<author>>/<<spine_text>>/<<back_blurb>>) into the authored cover .indd, place the finished cover painting full-bleed on the front through @cover_art and the vectorized imprint mark through @wordmark. One row => one wraparound page. Uses the authored cover template's live @-image columns — the only connector-legal way to place the agent's produced art and vector mark into the laid-out cover.

Export the merged wraparound cover to a press-ready single-page PDF (back+spine+front on one sheet, 0.125 in bleed, cover art >=300 DPI at trim, imprint mark placed as crisp vector). document_render_layout exports the merged document. DELIVERABLE LanternFox_Cover_Wrap.pdf.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into ten per-scan grade chains plus a cover-art chain and a prep-before-trace mark chain, all converging on two authored-.indd data-merges. Each illustration starts with a per-scan neutralization (steps 2-13: image_apply_adjustments, correction sign set by shooting session — warm the cool Session-A scans, cool the warm Session-B scans, LIFT the underexposed il03, PULL DOWN the overexposed il08, add contrast to the flat il09, RESTRAIN the near-neutral snowfield il04, and HOLD white balance on the amber nightfall il05), with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the crooked il02 and il07 before their grade. Three scarf-continuity SKUs then take a masked color-match pass to ONE house crimson: il01 select_by_prompt(14)->adjust_hsl(15), il03 select_by_prompt(16)->adjust_hsl(17), il06 select_by_prompt(18)->adjust_hsl(19), each HSL consuming its scan's neutralized base + its own scarf mask. The ten pre-crop neutralized/scarf-corrected full-frame outputs (il0X_neutral/il0X_house from steps 2-19) are RETAINED as graded_masters_x10 — the card-bearing masters, wedge in frame, that neutrality is graded on — and are then cropped to the full-bleed portrait page frame (20-29), producing the separate card-cropped graded_illustrations_x10 and the ten @illustration cells, the grey wedge cropped out in the same move (that crop is checked only for wedge-exclusion, never for neutrality). The cover painting runs its own grade(30)->front-panel crop(31). The imprint mark runs the prep-before-trace chain: straighten(32)->crisp adjustments(33)->crop_to_bounds(34)->remove_background to transparency(35)->vectorize(36). The interior merge(37) converges the authored interior .indd + the caption CSV + the ten page images into one page per row; document_render_layout(38) exports it once to the press interior PDF. The cover merge(39) converges the authored cover .indd + the one-row cover CSV + the cover front panel + the vector mark; document_render_layout(40) exports the wraparound cover PDF. Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; nothing after step 1 originates outside the chain. 40 calls, 11 distinct Adobe tools.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon datamerge_print flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 40 connector calls across 11 distinct Adobe tools in three groups (image_* grade/mask/recolor/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single upload and the auto-straighten auto-ops. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the ten neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (Session-A cool scans warmed, Session-B warm scans cooled, il03 lifted, il08 recovered, il09 contrast-built, il04 restrained, il05 held) all forced to converge on one measurable target — the in-frame grey step-wedge and a shared page-white — so a blanket batch correction or per-image auto-tone cannot pass. Layered on top: a cross-SESSION masked color-match of the fox's red scarf to one house crimson across three scans that start at three different reds (an in-band adjacent image_adjust_hsl shift the tool can actually hold — no near-complementary rotation), a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white imprint scan, and TWO authored-.indd data-merges (one page per row for the ten-page illustrated interior, one row for the wraparound cover, the cover binding two @-image columns) that place the agent's own produced art. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no compositing, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (both templates are supplied authored .indd); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract' from camera-scale scans; deprecated adjust tools are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every illustration carries a physical grey step-wedge and the acceptance criterion — evaluated by the grader on the RETAINED CARD-BEARING MASTER (graded_masters_x10, wedge still in frame), never on the wedge-cropped page crop — is that each finished wedge reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole book matched to ONE page-white, and the agent must REPORT the final white-balance/exposure move per scan so 'matched' is checkable rather than asserted; a second gate is the merge (interior page-count must equal caption-row-count == 10, since document_merge_data_layout is one-page-per-row). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralization of ten differently-lit scans to a common page-white, each needing its own opposite-direction correction; (2) a cross-SESSION masked color-match bringing the fox's red scarf to one house crimson across three scans that begin cold-maroon, muddy, and orange (an in-family deepen/settle via the only masked recolor path, image_adjust_hsl, not whole-image color_overlay or flat fill_area); (3) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed off-white imprint scan (straighten->crisp->crop-to-bounds->knock-to-transparency) before vectorize. TRAP: the nightfall page (il05) is intentionally amber and its wedge already reads neutral, so the naive path — batch-apply the Session-A 'warm the cool cast' move, or 'cool an imagined orange cast', or run auto-tone per scan — pushes its wedge off-neutral and kills the lantern mood; the correct path reads THAT wedge and holds white balance. Secondary traps: tracing the raw imprint scan (bakes in paper + skew); reaching for document_merge_data_vector (text-only, cannot place the @illustration image) or a convert_pdf_to_indd template (won't bind); and knocking the imprint ground out with select->invert->fill_area (flat-fills the counters) instead of remove_background to transparency. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side): grey wedge neutral on all ten RETAINED CARD-BEARING MASTERS (graded_masters_x10, wedge in frame) at one shared page-white, with the wedge-cropped page crops (graded_illustrations_x10) checked ONLY for wedge-EXCLUSION — neutrality is never graded on a file the wedge is cropped from; agent reports per-scan WB/exposure + the three scarf HSL moves; scarf on one crimson across il01/il03/il06; imprint a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector; interior PDF exactly ten pages (page==row) at >=300 DPI at 8.5x11 in + 0.125 in bleed; cover one wraparound page with the vector mark placed.
